docs.presetsPiles.component: Every game keeps stacks of things — a stock of cards, a tableau column, a poker bank of chips,
captured chess pieces, monopoly houses on a street — and every one of them is the SAME assembly.
`pile()` is that assembly as one literal of data: a seat, a box, a face, an arrangement by
registry name, and the four policies — what a finger may LIFT (`grab`), what may LAND (`accept`),
what the pile WEARS while willing (`invite`), and what SHADOW the resting stack lays (`shadow`).
```ts
import { pile, rect } from "game-kit"
const stock = pile("stock", {
bounds: rect(1, 1.4),
surface: "slot",
layout: "squared",     // a registry name the consumer registered
grab: "top",           // what a touch lifts
shadow: "silhouette",  // the stack casts once, as the wrap of what it holds
## Absence is the refusal
Every field but `layout` is optional, and leaving one out leaves its ATOM out: a pile with no
`grab` gives a finger nothing, a pile with no `accept` judges nothing, a pile with no `shadow`
casts nothing. There are no off-switches to disagree with the capabilities — the assembled node
either carries an atom or it does not.
## No behaviour lives here
The preset only composes: the grab is the `Grabber` registry's, the judgement is the `Acceptor`'s,
the glow rides the same invite bridge as any hand-built zone, and the shadow is the plan's own
stack-casts-once law. A new kind of pile — a discard that takes anything, a bank that gives one
chip — is a new LITERAL, never a new engine case.
docs.presetsPiles.piles: Three piles, three literals — there is no squared-pile class and no column class anywhere. The
squared stock answers a touch with its TOP card (`grab: "top"`), the column lifts the touched
card and everything above it (`"above"`), the fan gives exactly the card under the finger
(`"one"`). Drag off any of them: each pile lays ONE shadow for everything it holds, and a
lifted card starts casting its own the moment it stands alone on the desk.
